assessment.nobel_worthiness: The identification of distinct B- and T-cell lineages established a central organizing principle of adaptive immunity.
assessment.attribution: The two credited scientists represent complementary foundational contributions to defining lymphocyte lineages.
assessment.maturity: The principle has been deeply confirmed and remains fundamental to immunology and medicine.
uncertainties: The appropriate historical division of credit among contributors to lymphocyte biology remains broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response provided a major mechanistic account of how cells sense and respond to endoplasmic-reticulum stress.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter are strongly associated with defining key signaling mechanisms of the response.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is extensively established across cell biology, disease mechanisms, and physiology.
uncertainties: The breadth of the field makes the boundary between seminal and subsequent contributions difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chaperonin-assisted protein folding transformed understanding of how cells achieve productive protein conformation.
assessment.attribution: Horwich and Hartl are clear leading figures in the central experimental and conceptual advances.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is long established and has broad explanatory importance in cell biology and disease.
uncertainties: Protein-folding research includes additional contributors whose relative eligibility would require careful historical review.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Leptin revealed a decisive endocrine signal in the physiological control of appetite and body weight.
assessment.attribution: Friedman is directly and prominently associated with leptin's discovery and its physiological interpretation.
assessment.maturity: Its role in energy homeostasis is firmly established, despite the complexity of obesity biology.
uncertainties: Clinical translation to common obesity has been more limited than the discovery's physiological importance might suggest.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition made molecularly targeted cancer therapy a compelling clinical reality in chronic myeloid leukemia.
assessment.attribution: The credited names encompass drug development, clinical translation, and subsequent mechanistic therapeutic leadership.
assessment.maturity: The therapeutic paradigm has had durable, transformative benefit and extensive validation.
uncertainties: Attribution also implicates discovery of BCR-ABL and broader kinase-inhibitor development beyond the listed candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: VEGF biology and anti-VEGF therapy connected a fundamental angiogenic mechanism with major clinical advances.
assessment.attribution: The listed scientists capture key discovery and translational elements of the VEGF story.
assessment.maturity: Pathological angiogenesis and therapeutic inhibition are well established in ophthalmic and cancer medicine.
uncertainties: The exact allocation of credit between discovery, molecular characterization, and therapeutic development is complex.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics enabled causal, cell-type-resolved interrogation of physiological circuits and has changed experimental neuroscience.
assessment.attribution: The proposed laureates represent essential microbial-opsin and neurobiological implementation contributions.
assessment.maturity: The method is broadly adopted and its transformative experimental value is clear.
uncertainties: The candidate field contains several indispensable contributors, making a three-person attribution unusually difficult.
Long-term clinical significance remains less established than its research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fetal cell-free DNA in maternal blood enabled noninvasive prenatal screening and substantially changed prenatal diagnostics.
assessment.attribution: Lo is strongly identified with the foundational discovery and its development toward clinical use.
assessment.maturity: The principle has achieved wide clinical adoption and sustained validation.
uncertainties: Screening performance and implementation involve ethical and health-system questions distinct from the discovery itself.
